analysis:
The PR adds a selected-model recovery check to the capacity tick (ProviderLoop+Capacity.swift head line 82: `await checkSelectedModelRecoveryIfDue()`, placed after inventory registration and before superviseServingAuthorization/writeDaemonState). It also marks all recovery entries due after a successful unload or Nemotron Super retirement (ProviderLoop+ModelLoading.swift head ~1151-1155 and ~1219-1222).

The implementations of checkSelectedModelRecoveryIfDue and selectedModelRecovery.makeAllDue are not supplied.

Security-relevant expectations:
- Recovery loads should go through ensureModelLoaded (base 198-).
- That path keeps its existing guards: the autopilot selection check (base 213-216), the add-on hold fence (base 403, TB-012/T-059), native MiMo, GLM and retirement guards, the eviction gate and pending-load admission, and the weight-hash refresh before the slot goes active (T-012/T-027).
- makeAllDue only appears to change scheduling timing. It runs only after a retirement or unload succeeds, so it cannot be triggered across a trust boundary by consumers or providers. The add-on hold fence lives in ensureModelLoaded, so recovery loads cannot bypass it if routed there.

Availability concern: a recovery load or a `while` gate wait inside the tick (ensureModelLoaded can suspend on the load gate or MTP upgrade) could delay superviseServingAuthorization and the daemon-state write each tick. That matters to T-053/T-057 if recovery awaits a full model load inline. Integration should confirm that:
- checkSelectedModelRecoveryIfDue spawns or bounds its load work;
- it honours the addon hold and the allowEviction policy;
- it does not stall serving-authorization supervision.

No concrete regression was established from the visible evidence.
